test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The cost price of a toy is Rs. 210. What should be its MRP so that after a discount of 5% the shopkeeper gains 90%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MRP)** is given by the ratio:

**CP / MRP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Gain%)**

Ratio = (100 − 5) / (100 + 90) = 95 / 190 = 1 / 2

Since CP corresponds to 1 unit and is given as **Rs. 210**,

MRP corresponds to 2 units = 2 × 210 = **Rs. 420**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP = Rs. 210**, **Gain = 90%**, **Discount = 5%**.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) / 100 | MRP = SP × 100 / (100 − Discount%)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffd8fae8a41b72f0fa221a117e396cc3a6a64ca38bb7fabc93b94a9b63e1c898.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 210 × (100 + 90) / 100 = 210 × 1.9 = **Rs. 399**.
⇒ Let **MRP** be x. Discount is 5%, so 95% of x = SP.
⇒ 0.95 × x = 399
⇒ x = 399 / 0.95 = **Rs. 420**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price, while **Profit/Loss** is calculated on the Cost Price.

Relation Formula

MRP = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] / (100 − Discount%). This directly links CP and MRP when both profit and discount percentages are known.</p
